clue.text: Mothers getting over progeny's first illness

indicators.note: the mothers word gets over, that is covers round, the single letter that follows

parts.note: mums are mothers

indicators.note: this word picks out the opening letter, or opening letters, of the words it governs

explanation.surface: Mothers fret as their child falls ill for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting over' puts the first letter of 'progeny's' inside MUMS.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a viral infection with swollen glands, a common childhood complaint.

clue.text: Caravan owned by Alabama resident?

parts.note: Mobile is a city in Alabama, so a resident there might own a home named after the town; read plainly, a caravan is a dwelling on wheels

explanation.surface: A trailer belonging to someone living in a southern US state.
explanation.definitionFit: A large caravan used as a permanent dwelling goes by this name, and Mobile is an Alabama port city.

clue.text: Flirtatious woman, name drop ping to be sociable

indicators.note: dropping says the name letter falls out of the woman's word

parts.note: a minx is a pert, flirtatious girl

explanation.surface: A flirt forgets someone's name while trying to be friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: To mingle socially at a party is to circulate, chatting with the guests.

clue.text: Shame about line taken by cruel tyrant

indicators.note: about says the shame word goes round the line letter

parts.note: a stain on one's name is a shame or disgrace

explanation.surface: A disgrace accompanies the policy line of a brutal dictator.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet dictator was notorious for purges and terror, a byword for brutality.

clue.text: Wine used by clergymen is rough stuff

parts.note: sack is an old name for a dry white sherry-type wine
the cloth means the clergy collectively

explanation.surface: Communion wine for priests turns out to be coarse.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse fabric once worn in mourning or penance is literally rough material.

clue.text: Plant growing in wet soil, not dry stone

parts.note: sweet wine is the opposite of dry
a flag is a flagstone, a flat paving stone

explanation.surface: A gardener's note on what grows in damp earth rather than on a parched rock.
explanation.definitionFit: The calamus, an aromatic rush-like marsh plant, grows in boggy ground.

clue.text: Protective clothing for men

definitions.meaning: leather leggings worn by cowboys over trousers to protect the legs
fellows or blokes, in the informal British sense

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a cowboy's leather leg covers, and a colloquial word for fellows.

clue.text: Get ready to fire at ducks or another bird

parts.note: to cock a gun is to raise the hammer ready to shoot
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so ducks are two zeros, two Os

explanation.surface: A hunter primes a gun to shoot at waterfowl or some other bird.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of nought, hence O; 'ducks' gives two.
explanation.definitionFit: A crested parrot of Australia is a kind of bird.

clue.text: Travelling abroad's becoming unpopular

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both departing and going out of favour or fashion.

clue.text: Plugging extract from biography, perhaps

indicators.note: extract from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Promoting a book by quoting an excerpt from a life story.
explanation.definitionFit: Plugging a product is promoting it heavily, publicity of an exaggerated kind.

clue.text: Artist on TV appeared as creator of pictures

indicators.note: on, in this across clue, says the artist is placed following the television-and-appeared pieces

parts.note: the box is slang for television
came means turned up or appeared
RA is a Royal Academician, a recognised artist

explanation.surface: A painter turned up on television.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple early camera, a box-shaped device that takes photographs.

clue.text: Heartbroken after rent is raised

parts.note: rent here is the past of rend, torn or slashed
up means raised or lifted

explanation.surface: A tenant is devastated when the rent goes up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like housing payment, but it is the old past tense of rend, meaning torn.
explanation.definitionFit: Being deeply upset or distressed is informally described this way.

clue.text: Make satisfactory sort of cap, not like his

indicators.note: sort here works as a verb of arranging, so the following letters are put in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that a hat is not the style he wears.
explanation.definitionFit: To get something into good order or acceptable condition is an idiom for improving it.

clue.text: Feature of course on which you might see the Derby

definitions.text: Feature of course on which you might see the Derby

parts.words: Feature of course on which you might see the Derby
parts.note: the racecourse suggests horse racing, but Derby is also an English cheese, served at the cheese course of a meal

explanation.surface: Something at the racetrack where the famous horse race can be watched.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is England's most famous flat horse race; Derby is also a mild English cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A platter on which cheeses such as Derby are served is part of a meal's cheese course.

clue.text: Travelling round area in reconstructed inner city

indicators.note: in says the area letter goes inside the rebuilt letters
reconstructed says the two words that follow are rebuilt in a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tours a rebuilt part of the town centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reconstructed' turns INNERCITY into ITINERNCY, and 'in' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving from place to place, as a wandering preacher or tradesman does, is a life on the road.

clue.text: Philosopher's not good-hearted — a rotter, in fact

indicators.note: not, with hearted, says the good letter is dropped from the heart of the name

parts.note: Hegel was the German philosopher

explanation.surface: A thinker who is not kind turns out to be a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: '-hearted' says the G goes from the middle of HEGEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A cad or a scoundrel is a contemptible man.

clue.text: Husband installing son in accommodation that's ostentatious

indicators.note: in says that combination goes inside the accommodation word

parts.note: a flat is an apartment, a place to live

indicators.note: installing says the husband word takes the son word inside it

parts.note: a man is a husband, as in man and wife
a boy is a son

explanation.surface: A husband puts his boy up in a flashy apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husband' looks like the verb, to manage carefully, but it is the noun MAN; 'installing' and 'in' are the two container signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy and flashy behaviour or style is extravagantly eye-catching.

clue.text: Create impression, as some do in salon

definitions.meaning: cause a stir, disturb the status quo
a hairdresser may set curls or ripples in the hair

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both causing a disturbance and putting ripples into someone's hair.

clue.text: Two pans for this meat dish?

parts.note: a pan is a pot, a cooking vessel
to pan a show is to roast it, criticising harshly

explanation.surface: A recipe query: does this stew need two saucepans?
explanation.walkthrough: 'pans' gives two senses: a cooking vessel, and the verb to criticise.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef braised slowly in a covered vessel makes a classic meat dish.

clue.text: Modest christening for this composer

parts.note: Modest was the first name given to a Russian composer of Boris Godunov, so a modest naming is also literally his given name

explanation.surface: A low-key baptism held for a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Modest' looks like an adjective but is the composer's given name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian composer of Pictures at an Exhibition was christened Modest.

clue.text: I don't believe you can be such a twit

definitions.meaning: an expression of disbelief, like 'come off it'

explanation.definitionFit: As two words it is a cry of disbelief; as one word it means a silly fool.

clue.text: Rude programme heard but not seen

indicators.note: heard but not seen says only the sound of the programme word counts, not its spelling

parts.note: a course is a programme of study

explanation.surface: An offensive radio show is listened to but not watched.
explanation.definitionFit: Vulgar or crude language is impolite and offensive.

clue.text: Master of humorous fiction

parts.note: this looks like praise for a comic novelist, but it is the master served by a valet in P.G. Wodehouse's comic novels

explanation.surface: A tribute to a great comic writer.
explanation.walkthrough: In Wodehouse's stories the valet Jeeves serves an amiable young toff, his master.
explanation.definitionFit: The employer of Jeeves in the Wodehouse comic novels is literally a fictional master.

clue.text: Cold house, one associated with endless melancholy.

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: endless says the sadness word loses its final letter

parts.note: gloom is melancholy or sadness

explanation.surface: A chilly home where one person lives in constant sadness.
explanation.definitionFit: An Inuit dome dwelling built from snow blocks is a house in the cold.

clue.text: Take advantage of rich husband finally getting divorced

indicators.note: finally getting divorced says the husband letter is separated off from the end

parts.note: plush means luxurious or rich

explanation.surface: A gold-digger profits from a wealthy spouse when the divorce comes through.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefit or point in one's favour is an asset.

clue.text: Owns property in American city and one out East

indicators.note: in says the owning word goes inside the city letters

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
has means possesses or owns

explanation.surface: Someone holds real estate in a US city and another in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one out East' means another city, in the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tibetan capital is a city in the Orient.

clue.text: One tends to nag, being irritable with husband

parts.note: livery is an old word for liverish, bad-tempered
a man is a husband

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps griping is grumpy, as is her spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nag' means a horse, not to scold; a livery stable keeps horses for owners.
explanation.definitionFit: A keeper of a livery stable looks after horses kept there for owners.

clue.text: Low mark — the lowest possible, repeatedly

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

indicators.note: repeatedly says the zero letter appears twice

parts.note: zero, the letter O, is the lowest possible score

explanation.surface: A dreadful grade, the bottom score again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: A cow's call is a moo; to low is to make that sound.

clue.text: Disloyal doctor is outside

indicators.note: doctor as a verb means to tamper with, so the letters are altered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A treacherous physician waits out in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Inciting rebellion against the state is treacherous conduct.

clue.text: It's not part of the Black Forest, however

definitions.text: It's not part of the Black Forest, however

parts.words: It's not part of the Black Forest, however
parts.note: the Black Forest is a German woodland, yet a black wood from the tropics is no part of it

explanation.surface: A remark about a tree not found in the German woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: A dense black hardwood from tropical trees is black wood not grown in Germany.
